title: Manifest Approval Block
description: Forgery-resistant human-approval evidence for the Phase II->III/IV gate. Lives as the `approval` key inside contracts/MANIFEST.yaml. The gate NEVER trusts this block as a self-asserted fact: every field is a pointer to an externally verifiable signature, and the gate re-verifies mechanically on every transition. See references/approval-verification.md and SKILL.md rule #3. Deliberately has NO `verified`/`approved` boolean -- such a field would be agent-forgeable and load-bearing, which is exactly what this design forbids.

approver.description: Human approver identity (informational/audit). Trust derives from the signature, not this string.

approved_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp the approval was issued (informational; the signed git object carries the authoritative time).

manifest_hash.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the manifest with the `approval` block removed (see references/approval-verification.md). This is the exact value the approver signed; it transitively binds contract bodies via per-contract content hashes recorded in the manifest.

method.description: Verification mechanism. git-signed-tag is canonical. detached-signature (GPG/minisign/ssh over manifest_hash) is the non-git fallback. An unsigned / agent-authorable approval is NOT a valid method.

ref.description: git tag name or commit-ish for the signed object, e.g. modernize/approve/<run_id>/<short_hash>; or the detached-signature artifact path.

object.description: Immutable object id the ref resolved to at approval time (tag/commit SHA). Recorded so later drift in a mutable ref is detectable.

signing_key_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the key that produced the signature. MUST be on the configured approver allowlist (allowed-signers). e.g. SHA256:... for SSH, or a GPG long key id.

notes.description: Optional free-text approval notes (conditions, scope caveats).
